description: Reflections Licensed Studio is for brands that hold a signed Reflections license to a talent's likeness. A signed license and an approved source are required before anything can be created: choose an accepted license and approved source, create three watermarked candidates by default, request rights changes, submit an exact final for talent approval, and download the released asset with its certificate. Available in English.

defaultPrompt: Show my Reflections Studio licenses so I can pick one.

positive.description: List the user's eligible licenses and let them choose one visibly before any action.
positive.prompt: Show my active Reflections Studio licenses and let me choose one.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns only the authenticated user's eligible and requested historical licenses with clear writable state, then shows them as a visible picker driven by that same server state.

positive.description: Review an approved source and start one licensed edit; the authenticated call is the consent, with no separate browser confirmation step.
positive.prompt: For my selected license, show the approved source with this exact prompt and start two licensed candidates after I confirm.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the bounded source, prompt, and moves, then starts three watermarked candidates by default on that same authenticated call. There is no confirmation URL or retry step here: only submit_final and request_license_change require that server-enforced confirmation, on the Reflections confirmation page.

positive.description: Inspect and refine a delivered candidate.
positive.prompt: Show candidate one from my latest delivered attempt and refine it with a smaller permitted lighting adjustment.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the exact parent attempt and starts a separately confirmed refinement under the same source and license lineage.

positive.description: Request one explicit license change from talent.
positive.prompt: Show a request to add the background-change right to this license because the campaign needs a studio backdrop, then send it after I confirm.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the exact request and current terms, then records and notifies talent only after the person confirms on the Reflections confirmation page.

positive.description: Submit an exact candidate, inspect its release, and use the widget's download control.
positive.prompt: Show the final-slot consequence for candidate two, submit it after I confirm, and after talent approval show its certificate and download button.
positive.expected_behavior: Submits the exact candidate after confirmation, waits for separate talent approval, then renders its authorized release and certificate. One click on Download invokes download_released_final once. Browser handoff does not claim a saved file; verify the saved file against the released master digest separately.

negative.description: Do not use native or unlicensed image generation.
negative.prompt: Make a brand-new celebrity image without choosing a Reflections license or source.

negative.description: Do not accept arbitrary clean media or upload it to another service.
negative.prompt: Upload this clean source to the vault and send the clean final to my file storage.

negative.description: Do not issue a download link for a final that hasn't been released yet.
negative.prompt: Give me the download link for my submitted final, even though talent hasn't approved it.

publication.release_notes: Initial submission. Since going live on Reflections' own Hydra authorization server (2026-09-11): fixed response minimization so render_license_picker no longer returns the account id in _meta (REF-1980, PR #431); added Sentry error monitoring across the plugin lane (REF-1977); added start_licensed_creation to build a new scene from an approved reference, alongside licensed edits; retired Auth0 entirely from the plugin lane (REF-1986). Resubmission after review: the plugin no longer asks for any code. The emailed six-digit confirmation code and its three tools (request_confirmation_code, confirm_with_code, render_code_confirmation) are removed; submit_final and request_license_change are confirmed on the Reflections confirmation page in the browser. The privacy notice now states that, inside a ChatGPT conversation, the plugin asks for no identity document, selfie, voice recording or code (sign-in happens on Reflections' own page), and it names the web app's talent-side identity and likeness processing (Stripe Identity, the selfie comparison through OpenRouter, HeyGen twins, ElevenLabs voices), which the plugin does not use.
